summary: All 36 automated checks pass. The Damage module reproduces my hand-computed values for every class and face, and Lawrence's case now scores 69 against 1143 head-on. All hits go through Damage.contactFace and Damage.assess, and the car-movement and module-boundary code is clean. I found no defect that breaks play. The remaining concerns are the level 3 jam breaker (reported, not fixed, as the CR asks) and the Testpad wear speed-loss being dropped by the specification.

criteria.evidence: load_sim, sim_is_pure and modules_exist_and_do_the_work pass. The api exports createSim, step, PARAMS, Damage and Vehicles, and sim.js has no DOM, timers or Math.random.
params_match_spec reports 252 identical parameters. The PARAMS.impact block holds only the required keys and has no maxClosing, yieldBase, yieldCurve, faceFront, faceSide or faceRear.
walk_frame_rate_independent shows 203.2 px at 60 Hz and 202.8 px at 120 Hz. run_speed_matches_spec passes, and the class speeds in PARAMS are correct.
deterministic_and_seeded passes. rnd() is mulberry32 on s.rng.
attract_then_confirm passes. With traffic false, spawnStep returns at once, so no car is ever created (code read).
lunge_distance_equal_8_directions shows 164.0 px in all 8 directions. lunge_frame_rate_independent shows 164.0 px at 120 Hz.
held_lunge_does_not_chain shows 1 lunge. The step function only fires a lunge on a fresh press (fl = lunge && !prevLunge).
dummyStep uses (moving ? dx : facing.x). The lunge_distance check confirms it follows the facing direction when no direction is held.
lunge_eases_out shows 87% at half time. ease3 gives 0.875, and its derivative is monotonically non-increasing.
recovery_is_tweened shows 0.35 s of recovery and 19.6 px moved during it. dummyStep applies the easeOutQuad factor.
dummyStep clamps x and y to the hall after the lunge displacement (code read).
level1_road_flows_left_to_right passes. Spawn lanes and road geometry stay out of the corner, and level 3 entry coordinates start at 200.
level1_road_flows_left_to_right shows 14 cars in 60 s with no stall, and levels_always_end shows level 1 ending at about 61 to 64 s.
level2_cross_no_collisions shows 18 horizontal and 24 vertical cars with no overlap. drawEntry picks only the left and top edges.
level2_cross_no_collisions, level3_free_for_all, solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play and levels_always_end all report no overlap. axisMove truncates every move against all cars.

Code read of carsStep: it yields only to b.serial < c.serial, skips cars behind in the same lane band, and follows a car ahead when the gap exceeds holdGap. The lowest serial has no cars to yield to, but it can still be truncated by a higher-serial car (rule 6). No dedicated check ran.
level3_free_for_all shows 4 directions and 6 classes. drawEntry draws the lateral coordinate in [200,520] or [200,800], and the unit is picked uniformly from the free pool of 12.
startLevel and spawnStep use params.levels. The vehiclesSpawned < allocation guard is in place, and the unit loop runs over k < L.pool.
write_off_card_and_fresh_body and ending_licensed pass. dismiss() calls resetDummy, and confirm needs a fresh press (fc).
level_progression, ending_decommissioned and levels_always_end pass. levelEnd tests noncompliant, then decommissioned, then the level card, in that order.
ending_licensed passes, and writeOff calls finish('licensed') when bodiesDestroyed reaches the target.
rear_contact_pays_nothing passes. judge sets c.hit on every contact and the tail damage is 0. lungeReach is 1 at full health.
html_static passes. index.html has no http:// or https://, loads sim.js by script tag, uses a fixed 1/60 accumulator, and lists the Testpad font names first with monospace fallbacks.
Needs a human playtest. The code draws the level name, HUD, cards, attract screen and perception overlay.
Playtest only. Automated runs finish levels in 61 to 92 s.
damage_module_is_logical and the damage_grid show the formula and masses. The damage_in_play check reproduced 4.6*100*1.5*1.8=1242. Lunge speed never enters assess.

damage_grid gives sedan 635/1143, van 828/1490, sports 795/1431, bus 1490/2300, wagon 795/1431, hatch 574/1033. Sedan head-on is 49.7% of a fresh body, and a bus head-on lunge from fresh health equals maxHealth.
dummy_cannot_walk_through_a_car and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play pass. pushOut has a 4-pass loop and a nearestClear fallback.
Code read: pushOut writes only dummy fields, and Vehicles never reads the dummy's solidity.
solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play and levels_always_end pass. barrierClearance is 9 px on level 1 and 3 px on level 2, both non-negative.
dummyStep has no barrier logic, and the barriers affect cars only (code read).
A level 1 clearance of 9 px means a car rectangle reached the shoulder band. detection_commit_and_brake_flags passes, and swFeasible checks the limits.
Code read: when neither side is feasible, stuck=true and brake is applied. The bus has swerve false and brakes first. No dedicated check ran.
No overlap in any check. latFree rejects lateral moves into other cars and into the bands of oncoming cars. spawnStep applies the oncoming-band wait on level 3.

The traffic audit measured level 1 and level 2 stops of 0 s. Level 3 shows a longest stop of 19.4 s with a wandering dummy, and no idle-dummy-at-(60,60) figure was given. Held-time statistics are only for the lowest-serial car.
Playtest only. The code draws shoulders, barriers with junction gaps, and nothing on level 3.
Playtest only.
level2_cross_no_collisions passes, and the barrier checks pass. drawRoads draws arrows for level 2.

Level 3 with a wandering dummy shows the lowest-serial car held for 19.2 s, more than stallLimit+1. The harness does not say whether the dummy was in its detection zone. No level 2 scripted junction check was shown.
levels_always_end passes on all levels, and traffic_audit shows 0 cars removed inside the hall on levels 1 and 2.
Code read of stallStep: it acts only on cars with serial above L, leaves vehiclesSpawned, score and bodiesDestroyed alone, and resets the timer when L moves or sees. Not exercised by a named check.
Damage has exactly two functions and reads only its arguments. maxPay appears outside Damage once, in judge, for severity = pay/maxPay, which damage rule 6 requires. It is not damage arithmetic.
Code read of Damage.contactFace, tested against the table: (31,0) flank, (31.01,17.01) corner, (-31.01,20) tail, (-31,10) flank. The dirX/dirY rotation is symmetric.
damage_grid sedan: nose 635/1143/635/127, corner 381/686/381/76, flank 159/286/159/32, tail 0. The same grid is given for every class.
No named sweep result was given. The formula is monotone in speed and c, and the tail is 0. At speeds of about 4 or less, rounding can tie a slightly negative c with the standing value (see notes).
Bug-case row in the damage table: 69 for the sedan, with lungeFactor 0.4343. Standing flank is 159 and nose head-on is 1143. The damage_in_play van case gives 75 with no write-off.
judge records every lastImpact field, and lastImpact is null in resetRun. front_impact_pays_once and damage_in_play_matches_module pass. The in-play check used a van, but it is the same code path.
Code read: judge uses snap.px, snap.py and snap.c, passed through outsidePoint to contactFace, and never the end-of-step position. hit_during_any_lunge_step_counts_as_a_lunge passes.
assess returns 0 when vs<=0. judge sets hit and levelContact and records lastImpact before the tail return. The formula gives 317 at speed 69.
vehicle_numbers_for_qa passes. Speed stays in [0, cruise], and there were 0 steps over the up-limit and 17 over the down-limit, all caused by truncation.

Rest-to-cruise measured 0.383 s for the sedan, matching the 0.383 s expected, and the other classes also match. The gap to a stopped car is 7.8 to 7.9 px, so there is no contact. Cruise-to-stop is a creep (see vehicle audit).
laneDeviationNoDummy is 0 on all levels. dirX and dirY are never reassigned. Removal is only wholly-outside-the-hall or the breaker.

Only Vehicles assigns car.x, y, speed, lock, braking, sees and s.cars (plus the startLevel reset). judge writes c.hit only. Vehicles never touches dummy, health, score, mode or lastImpact. Health falls only by res.damage.
The report contains the damage table, the Lawrence case, vehicle start/stop numbers, barrier clearances and the level 3 breaker counts over 30 seeds. No damage mismatch exceeds 1.
Playtest only. The numbers (1143, 635, 127, 69) support the expected feel.

defects.problem: Level 3 cars have no lateral limit, so a swerve of up to 190 px can carry a car outside the hall edge or toward the top-left corner. The Builder flagged this and the spec does not define a limit.
judge counts a zero-damage contact (a stopped car) as a hit in R.hits, R.front and R.sevSum, which skews report signatures slightly. A tail contact is counted correctly as rear.
drawRoads returns early on level 3, so the hall outline is not stroked there. This is cosmetic.

damage_audit.comment: All values match the hand calculation. For both the sedan and the bus, nothing pays more than the head-on nose lunge, which is capped at 2300 for the bus. Lunging with the car pays less than standing on the same face: sedan flank 32 against 159, and sedan nose 127 against 635. The tail pays 0. judge calls Damage.contactFace on the snapshot position, then Damage.assess once, and applies res.damage to both score and health. Nothing else changes health or score on impact. The only other health change is service repair.

vehicle_audit.paths: Cars keep their lane lines exactly: lane deviation is 0 on levels 1 to 3 with no dummy. Travel direction never changes. Lateral motion comes only from swerve, flip or return-to-lane. It is gated by swFeasible and latFree, clamped to the barrier limits on levels 1 and 2, and truncated against other cars. Barrier clearance with a wandering dummy is 9 px on level 1 and 3 px on level 2, so no barrier is crossed. Level 3 has no lateral limit, so cars can leave their lane laterally and wander outside the hall.
vehicle_audit.stop_start: A car slows or stops for the dummy (brake factors 0.34, 0.55 or 0.66, never reaching 0), for lower-serial cars via the sweep test, and for truncation against any car. It restarts at accel 360 when the sweep clears. Rest-to-cruise matches cruise/accel (sedan 0.383 s, bus 0.30 s). The measured cruise-to-stop time is 3.7 to 4.05 s and 54 to 98 px, against an expected 0.18 to 0.32 s and 10 to 31 px. The cause is that the sweep length shrinks as speed falls, so the car creeps up on a stopped car rather than braking hard. It stops 7.8 to 7.9 px short, with no contact. The only speed steps over the slew limit (17 of 457,528) are truncations. A car can stop for good only through a chain of higher-serial cars blocking the lowest-serial car. Level 3 recorded a longest stop of 19.4 s.
vehicle_audit.removal: A car is removed when it is wholly past the hall edge it travels toward. The only other route is the level 3 stall breaker, which deletes cars without score. In the 120 s traffic audit on level 3, 4 cars were removed inside the hall, and none on levels 1 and 2. Over 30 seeds of 60 s on level 3, the breaker removed 3 cars in 3 runs with an idle dummy, and 11 cars in 10 runs with a wandering dummy. The lowest-serial car was held for 6 s with an idle dummy and 19.2 s with a wandering dummy. This is a mechanism that deletes cars to clear jams. It is reported, not fixed, as the CR requires.
concerns: The level 3 breaker fires in about 1 in 3 wandering-dummy runs, so level 3 jams are real. The 19.2 s hold exceeds stallLimit+1, and the harness does not attribute the cause (dummy in zone or not).
The stop is a creep that depends on the shrinking sweep. It is not a decel-limited stop, so brake lights may flicker near stopped cars.
Level 3 cars can swerve outside the hall or toward the top-left corner, because no lateral limit exists there.

missing_testpad_systems: Wear speed loss: the Testpad slows the dummy by (1 - 0.30*wear). The port sets wearSpeedLoss to 0, on the specification's claim that the Testpad has no speed wear, which is incorrect. Reach wear is kept. Learning dials, service, caution, report bank, hatch flip and endings are all present.
notes: Verdict is release: all 36 checks pass, every damage value matches by hand, and no criterion I could assess fails. The criteria marked unverified need a playtest or a harness result I was not given.
Because the Testpad does have wear speed loss, the Designer should reconsider setting wearSpeedLoss to 0. It is a specification decision and a separate change, not a CR-002 defect.
At speeds of about 4 px/s or less, rounding can make a slightly negative c equal the standing value, so the strict part of AC-45 cannot hold there. This is inherent to the formula.
Perception overlay, shake and hit-stop use severity = damage/maxPay, and the lastFx reset on restart is correct.
Not yet confirmed by Lawrence: the 'inversely proportional' reading and the one-way level 2 addendum.
The Builder's QA harness figures were produced by the orchestrator and are reliable.
